numbers.note: 62000 steps in 0.31 s of wall clock, one particle, on trap_hoomd_backend -- the same builder this configuration runs on with the flow removed. MEASURED at N=1, which the driven configuration's budget had to bracket across three decades before this run existed

numbers.name: steps_max_per_point
numbers.note: the share of the local wall clock one sweep point may spend, as steps. No formula: the ceiling is the person's decision and 5.3 has no source kind for one; the arithmetic is in the rationale

numbers.name: thermal_width_op
numbers.note: THE PREDICTION: the per-axis width equipartition gives at this stiffness. Both the run and the bench are compared against it, and the bench's deviation from it is what yields the stiffness

numbers.name: integration_timestep_op

numbers.name: save_interval_op

numbers.name: startup_discard_op
numbers.note: the particle starts at the trap centre and its distribution relaxes over gamma/k_t; ten of them leave a residual far below a per mille. Declared in advance, never chosen after seeing the data

numbers.name: record_length_op

numbers.name: width_bias_op

numbers.name: width_scatter_op

numbers.name: width_acceptance_op
numbers.note: the success band, three of the record's own standard errors, fixed before the run

numbers.name: camera_exposure_max_op
numbers.note: the longest bench exposure that keeps exposure averaging under three per cent of the variance (A4's precondition); a longer one needs the correction applied to the simulated width

numbers.name: particle_step_rate

numbers.name: particle_steps_op

assumptions.statement: The double well's soft trap, 0.5 pN/um, is the one stiffness this revision runs, because it is the first input the double well needs.
assumptions.falsifier: the bench reporting that its lowest usable dial setting is far stiffer moves it

assumptions.statement: A tenth of the thermal width per step. Dependent on the relaxation bound only because the declared potential is exactly harmonic; a trap that flattens away from its centre would separate them again.
assumptions.falsifier: a non-quadratic trap makes this a distinct bound

assumptions.statement: A hundred relaxation times: long enough that the width's bias is a per cent and its scatter under a tenth, both far inside the one decade the goal asks for. A convention, and the record a per-cent stiffness would need is the relation in the note, not this number.
assumptions.falsifier: a first run whose measured width is still rising between half the record and the whole of it falsifies the bias estimate and lengthens the record

assumptions.statement: A tenth of the relaxation time resolves the autocorrelation whose shape the A2 scatter assumes, which is the one thing a run can check about its own statistics.
assumptions.falsifier: a first run whose measured autocorrelation is flat between a tenth and a half of tau_t loosens it

assumptions.statement: Two hours from envelope/budget.json over the measured 5 us a step over 4 stiffness points: 7200 / 5e-6 / 4, about 360000000 steps a point, to one figure. A point needs about 1e4 steps, so the budget is not the constraint anywhere here.
assumptions.falsifier: this question's own first run replaces the prior run's cost

kb_refs.claim: The particles in the bottle in use have a diameter of 5 micrometres, with a coefficient of variation no greater than 2 per cent, measured directly by the operator on 2026-09-19.
Dynamic viscosity of pure water near 293 K is of order one millipascal second, and it changes by roughly two percent per kelvin in that neighbourhood.

The expected translational diffusivity of a tracer sphere in a bulk fluid is the Stokes-Einstein value, k_B T over 3 pi eta d. It is a prediction from the viscosity, the temperature and the diameter, not a measurement of how the particles actually move.

The laboratory's ambient temperature is 20 degrees Celsius, read off a thermometer by the operator. It is a reading and not a setpoint, and it is the room's rather than the sample's -- which is what makes it an operator reading at E3 and not a calibration at E2.
There is no thermometer beside the sample. The only thermometer in the laboratory reads the room, so any temperature attributed to the sample is a room reading applied to it.
The room is held continuously by air conditioning. There is a setpoint on this instrument's environment -- it is the room's, not the sample's.
